title: Immersive and Personalized Virtual Reality for Women's Well-Being During Childbirth
official: Immersive and Personalized Virtual Reality for Women's Well-Being During Childbirth: Proof of Concept and Feasibility Study With Women in the Prodromal Phase and the First Stage of Labor
summary: This study evaluates the feasibility, acceptability, and potential use of personalized immersive virtual reality environments (iVRe) as a non-pharmacological support for managing pain and anxiety during the prodromal phase and first stage of labor. iVRe provides realistic or customizable visual and auditory experiences tailored to individual preferences, aiming to promote relaxation, cognitive distraction, engagement, and a greater sense of control during childbirth. The project is integrated into an obstetric care model that prioritizes a positive birth experience and personalized, natural pain-management strategies. Although previous research suggests that virtual reality may reduce pain and anxiety in medical settings and during labor, evidence remains limited, particularly in Italy. The main objective is therefore to determine whether customizable iVRe can be safely and appropriately introduced into childbirth care. The study will also identify the most suitable stages of labor for headset use, potential barriers and facilitators to implementation, and the visual, auditory, and usage features considered most effective in promoting relaxation, well-being, and pain management. The project includes two preliminary exploratory phases. The first involves obstetric and gynecological healthcare professionals who routinely assist women during labor and childbirth. Following a VR exposure session, standardized questionnaires and a focus group will assess feasibility, usability, sense of presence, possible side effects, and methodological considerations for future implementation with women in labor. The second phase involves women approximately 40 days postpartum. Drawing on their recent childbirth experience, participants will evaluate the acceptability of VR and provide suggestions regarding its use. The assessment will include emotional state before and after exposure, headset-related symptoms, usability, engagement, realism, and preferences for virtual content. Expected outcomes include preliminary evidence on the safety, tolerability, usability, and acceptability of immersive VR in obstetric care. These findings will be used to refine the methodology and procedures for a subsequent study involving women during the prodromal phase and labor.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Postpartum Women Feasibility Group
* Women who gave birth approximately 40 days before enrollment and attend the routine postpartum follow-up visit at the family counseling center.
* Native Italian speakers.
* Able and willing to provide written informed consent.
* Healthcare Staff Feasibility Group.
* Healthcare professionals working at the Obstetrics and Gynecology Unit of Santa Chiara Hospital in Trento.
* Healthcare professionals who routinely support and assist women during labor and childbirth.
* Native Italian speakers.
* Able and willing to provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of epilepsy or first-degree relatives with a diagnosis of epilepsy.
* Presence of a cardiac pacemaker or other metallic devices.
* Active infectious or gastrointestinal disorders.
* Presence of open wounds on the face.
* Motor or visual impairments that prevent use of the virtual reality headset.
* Neuromuscular pain that prevents use of the virtual reality headset.
* Refusal or inability to provide written informed consent for study participation.
